title: Trump admin to receive $100 million in compute credits for AI science initiative
source_used: Politico (original blocked here: HTTP 403); read through Business Insider's copy of the Politico story, which carries the Politico credit
key_facts: National Compute, a new company that has pooled computing power from major tech companies, plans to donate $100 million worth of computing credits to the Trump administration.
The credits would support the Genesis Mission, a government-wide push to use AI to accelerate scientific discovery.

The donation is expected to be announced Thursday at an event with White House Office of Science and Technology Policy Director Michael Kratsios, according to two people familiar with the matter who were not authorised to discuss it.
The donation would give Genesis Mission researchers access to advanced computing when smaller labs and companies can struggle to secure capacity for frontier research.
National Compute is building the National Compute Grid, a network meant to pool computing capacity from several providers and make it available to researchers, companies and government agencies.
A draft paper explaining the project, reviewed by Politico, compares the grid to the power grid or the interstate highway system.
